comparison: Perfect agreement on dynamical systems analysis (C47-C55). Both evaluations strongly support the fixed point identification, ring attractor interpretation, and funneling dynamics. Peer reviewers specifically praise this as 'a model for how to reverse engineer and mechanistically understand computation in RNNs.'

Both address biological data reanalysis (C75-C80, C103) but with different levels of certainty. OpenEval finds the analysis methodologically sound despite small sample size. Peer reviewers express reservations about incomplete comparisons between RNN and biological analyses, and note that 5/18 biological pairs don't show alignment as predicted.

Both evaluate quantitative RNN-biology comparison (C21-C23, C108-C114). OpenEval views the firing rate discrepancy (1.9-fold vs 1.28-fold) as honest limitation assessment. Peer reviewers are more uncertain, suggesting regularization might address this gap and make models more biologically realistic.

Strong agreement on multi-map generalization (C65-C74). Both evaluations support the scalability findings and building block concept (C101-C102). OpenEval emphasizes empirical demonstration across all metrics. Peer reviewers highlight this as demonstrating generalization beyond experimental conditions.

Strong agreement on 2D generalization (C56-C64, C4, C83). Both evaluations affirm that the model successfully extends to 2D environments with preserved geometric principles. Peer reviewers note this demonstrates the simplicity and generality of the proposed mechanisms.

Strong agreement on core RNN remapping findings (C3, C18-C20, C24-C28). OpenEval emphasizes converging quantitative evidence. Peer reviewers describe the results as 'strongly supported and convincing' with 'rigorous and careful analysis' and 'state of the art' methods. Both note the biological relevance.

Agreement on theoretical predictions about orthogonal organization (C29-C33). OpenEval finds the theoretical motivation sound and empirically confirmed. Peer reviewers accept the framework, noting it enables 'compositional computation with valuable properties for shared and distinct readouts.'

Strong agreement on theoretical insight that alignment is not task-required (C36-C40). Both evaluations praise the demonstration that alignment emerges rather than being imposed. Peer reviewers specifically highlight the 'particular care' taken to show this is not a necessary consequence of model design.

Agreement on manifold alignment findings (C44-C46). OpenEval notes the empirical support and appropriate acknowledgment of imperfect alignment. Peer reviewers affirm this, praising the clarification of scenarios where weaker alignment could occur and noting the simplicity of the solution.

Agreement on orthogonalization principle (C34-C35, C82). OpenEval finds the empirical confirmation sound. Peer reviewers accept without critique and specifically highlight the 'compositional organization' as a key strength, supporting that orthogonalization prevents interference.

Agreement on contextualization within RNN literature (C98-C99, C100). Both evaluations support the citations to prior work on modularity. Peer reviewers explicitly connect findings to broader literature on remapping as input-driven state space shifts.

Different evaluation types for forward-looking claims (C104-C107, C81, C95, C105, C107). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, affirming the normative contribution and stating the work 'offers both a normative explanation' and 'provides evidence that RNNs can investigate neural mechanisms.'

Overlap on summary claims (C81-C83, C100-C102). OpenEval finds these well-supported by detailed results. Peer reviewers strongly affirm the normative framework, with all three reviewers praising the mechanistic insights and theoretical contributions.

Partial overlap on building block concept (C101-C102). OpenEval views this as reasonable inference from generalization results. Peer reviewers support this through discussion of symmetric organization and contextual input effects across multiple contexts.

OpenEval evaluates background claims (C1-C2, C5-C9) as well-supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel contributions rather than established background.

OpenEval evaluates prior work characterization (C10-C17) as appropriately cited and accurate. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not separately assess literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates broader literature contextualization (C84-C97) as accurate and fair. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers implicitly accepted the framing by not challenging it.
